newsitem.title: FRANCE: France holds seven in swoops on Corsican suspects.
newsitem.headline: France holds seven in swoops on Corsican suspects.

text.p: French police on Thursday rounded up 12 people suspected of helping Corsican separatists bomb the mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux two weeks ago, the Interior Ministry said.
But justice sources later said the five women among those arrested were released while seven men remained in police custody.

The ministry said police, including an elite anti-terrorist unit, swooped simultaneously on suspects in the town of Bonifacio, on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica, and around the southern mainland cities of Bordeaux and Marseille.
Two of the women were brought for questioning in Bonifacio, two near Bordeaux and one in Marseille, the sources said.
Police also seized weapons during Thursday's swoops.

The police action, the largest in years in connection with an upsurge in separatist violence in Corsica, appeared intended to demonstrate the prime minister's determination to firmly apply the law on the island.
Critics had predicted the Juppe government would not confront the separatist movement for fear of triggering spiraling guerrilla violence.

The "historic wing" of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) has claimed responsibility for the Bordeaux bombing, as well as for two later bombings of official buildings in the southern mainland town of Nimes.

The mainland attacks were a big escalation by separatists whose two-decade-old campaign for greater autonomy from France had been confined to hundreds of mostly small bombings in Corsica over the past few years.

Justice sources said that those held were close to the leader of the political wing of the FLNC, Francois Santoni, who was sentenced earlier this month in his absence to four months in jail for carrying guns.
Santoni is still in hiding. But among those arrested in Marseille were members of a family who have served as his bodyguards, the sources said.

One of those arrested in Corsica was a boatman, the sources said. A huge contingent of police helped in the arrest, including some on boats offshore to prevent the man from fleeing by sea, the sources said.
The interior ministry did not identify the detainees, but said they could have helped with the logistics for the attack on the Bordeaux city hall, which caused significant damage but no injuries.

The arrests were carried out on the orders of the country's senior anti-terrorist investigating judge, Jean-Louis Bruguiere, who was placed in charge of the probe when Juppe ordered a crackdown on Corsican guerrillas.

Juppe vowed anew to apply the law in Corsica and crack down on guerrillas after the FLNC warned him against any attempt to "physically eliminate" its members, saying its response would be of an "incalculable violence".
